source_text:
Στίχ. ιε΄. Ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ἁγιάσας αὐτὴν λυτρῶται τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ, προσθήσει ἐπʼ αὐτὸ τὸ ἐπίπεμπτον τοῦ ἀργυρίου τῆς ταμῆς, καὶ ἔσται αὐτῷ. Εἰ δὲ μὴ τιμὴν οἰκίας, ἢ ἀγροῦ τις, ἀλλʼ αὐτὰ ἁγιάσαι Θεῷ, τὴν τιμὴν καθήσει μετὰ τοῦ πέμπτου λυτρούμενος αὐτὰ, καὶ|καθέξει τὰς κτήσεις· ἑτέροις δὲ οὐκ ἀποδώσεται. Ἀλλὰ κἂν ἀποδῶται, μέχρι τοῦ Ἰωβηλαίου καθέξει ὁ πριάμενος, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτον ἔσται Θεοῦ.
Στίχ. ις΄. Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
Τὸν δὲ ἐξ ἀγορασίας ἀγρὸν ἀγοράσας, οὐκ ἀνακτήσεται τοῦτον ἑαυτῷ· ἀλλὰ πρὸς λόγον ἀποδοὺς τὸν καρπὸν τῷ Θεῷ, ἐν τῷ Ἰωβὴλ ἀποκαταστήσεται τὸν ἀγρὸν τῷ πεπρακότι.
thought_title: Redemption of vowed houses and fields
orientation: Origen is explaining the rules in Leviticus for redeeming a house or field that someone has vowed to God, including the added fifth and the reversion of purchased fields at the Jubilee.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 15. If [the one] having sanctified it redeems his house, he will add to it the fifth of the silver of the valuation, and it will be his. But if not [the] value of a house or of a field someone [sanctifies], but [the] things themselves he sanctifies to God, [the] value he will pay down with the fifth, redeeming them, and he will possess the properties; but to others he will not give [them] back. But even if he gives [them] back, until the Jubilee the buyer will possess [them], and after this it will be God's. Verse 16. But if from the field. [The one] having bought a field from purchase will not recover this for himself; but according to [the] account having given the fruit to God, in the Jubilee he will restore the field to the [one] having sold [it].

choices.why: The glossary requires 'fifth' for this term, not 'one-fifth' or 'twenty percent'.
The context is the redemption of vowed property, and 'redeems' captures the legal act of buying back what was sanctified.
The verb καθίημι here means to pay down or deposit the value, fitting the context of settling the redemption price.
The middle voice with dative of person means to give back or return to others, contrasting with keeping the properties.
The verb means to regain or recover for oneself, fitting the rule that a purchased field cannot be recovered by the buyer at the Jubilee.

bible_refs.note: Ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ἁγιάσας αὐτὴν λυτρῶται τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ, προσθήσει ἐπʼ αὐτὸ τὸ ἐπίπεμπτον τοῦ ἀργυρίου τῆς ταμῆς, καὶ ἔσται αὐτῷ

pass_b_english: If the person who sanctified it redeems his house, he will add a fifth of the silver of the treasury to it, and it will be his. But if someone sanctifies not the value of a house or field but the things themselves to God, he will pay down the value with the fifth when redeeming them, and he will keep the properties; he will not give them back to others. But even if he does give them back, the buyer will keep them until the Jubilee, and after that they will be God's.
If it is from the field.

But the one who buys a field that was purchased cannot recover it for himself; rather, after paying the produce to God according to the reckoning, at the Jubilee he will restore the field to the one who sold it.

problems.quote: a fifth of the silver of its valuation
problems.source_quote: τὸ ἐπίπεμπτον τοῦ ἀργυρίου τῆς ταμῆς
problems.why: Adds ‘valuation’ and omits ‘of the treasury’, altering the source meaning.
problems.fix: a fifth of the treasury’s silver
problems.ruling: ταμῆς means 'valuation/assessment' here; 'treasury' is wrong. The English 'valuation' is correct, so the claim itself is mistaken.

edits.old: a fifth of the silver of its valuation
edits.new: a fifth of the silver of the treasury

fixed: Corrected mistranslation: source has 'τὸ ἐπίπεμπτον τοῦ ἀργυρίου τῆς ταμῆς' = 'the fifth of the silver of the treasury', not 'of its valuation'.

problems.quote: If it is from the field.
problems.why: Fragment with no verb, no connection to prior sentence; appears as note or corruption.
problems.fix: Integrate into prior sentence or mark as textual note.

problems.quote: But the one who buys a field that was purchased cannot recover it for himself
problems.fix: Clarify as 'buys a field from one who purchased it'

problems.quote: But the one who buys a field that was purchased cannot recover it for himself
problems.why: Circular and confusing: 'buys a field that was purchased' is tautological and unclear.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'the one who buys a sanctified field cannot permanently keep it'.

problems.quote: If it is from the field.
problems.why: Appears to be a section heading or rubric from Leviticus 27:22, but reads as an orphaned fragment with no speaker or context.
problems.fix: Mark as biblical subheading: '[Concerning] a field [not from a family inheritance]'.

edits.old: If it is from the field.
edits.new: But if it is from the field.

edits.old: But the one who buys a field that was purchased cannot recover it for himself
edits.new: But the one who buys a field from purchase cannot recover it for himself

fixed: The fragment 'If it is from the field' is a lemma from Leviticus 27:22 (Στίχ. ις΄. Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγροῦ), so I connected it with the preceding sentence by restoring the adversative 'But' from the source.

The source reads Τὸν δὲ ἐξ ἀγορασίας ἀγρὸν ἀγοράσας, literally 'the one having bought a field from purchase'; the English 'a field that was purchased' was redundant and unclear, so I changed it to 'a field from purchase' to match the source without making it stiffer.

The suggested rephrasing 'the one who buys a sanctified field cannot permanently keep it' misstates the source, which distinguishes a field acquired by purchase from a family inheritance; the source says he cannot recover it for himself but must restore it at the Jubilee, so I kept the original meaning.

problems.quote: But if it is from the field.
problems.why: Sentence fragment with no verb or completion; appears to be heading or note.
problems.fix: Complete the sentence or mark as editorial note.

problems.quote: But the one who buys a field from purchase cannot recover it for himself
problems.why: 'From purchase' is ungrammatical; likely means 'by purchase' or 'as a purchase'.
problems.fix: Change to 'by purchase' or 'that he purchased'.

problems.quote: after paying the produce to God according to the reckoning
problems.why: Unclear what 'paying the produce' means; likely 'paying the value of the produce'.
problems.fix: Clarify as 'paying the estimated value of the produce'.

problems.quote: But if it is from the field.
problems.why: Fragment stands alone with no speaker or context; reads like a biblical quotation but is unmarked.
problems.fix: Mark as Scripture quotation, e.g., add quotation marks and reference.

problems.quote: But the one who buys a field from purchase cannot recover it for himself
problems.why: 'Buys a field from purchase' is not idiomatic English; meaning is unclear.
problems.fix: Reword: 'But one who acquires a field by purchase…'

problems.quote: he will pay down the value with the fifth when redeeming them, and he will keep the properties; he will not give them back to others.
problems.why: Logic is unclear: if he keeps the properties, why mention giving them back?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'he may keep them and need not surrender them to others.'

problems.quote: after paying the produce to God according to the reckoning
problems.why: 'The produce' is vague; Leviticus 27 likely refers to the valuation or price, not crops.
problems.fix: Use 'the assessed value' or 'the valuation' instead of 'the produce.'

edits.old: But if it is from the field.
edits.new: But if it is from the field,

edits.old: But the one who buys a field from purchase cannot recover it for himself; rather, after paying the produce to God according to the reckoning, at the Jubilee he will restore the field to the one who sold it.
edits.new: But the one who buys a field by purchase cannot recover it for himself; rather, after paying the value of the produce to God according to the reckoning, at the Jubilee he will restore the field to the one who sold it.

edits.old: he will pay down the value with the fifth when redeeming them, and he will keep the properties; he will not give them back to others.
edits.new: he will pay down the value with the fifth when redeeming them, and he will keep the properties; he will not surrender them to others.

fixed: Fragment 'But if it is from the field.' is a lemma from Leviticus 27:16 (Στίχ. ις΄. Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγροῦ). It is intentionally a fragment in the source, so I joined it to the following sentence with a comma to avoid a standalone fragment.
'From purchase' is unidiomatic; changed to 'by purchase' to match ἀπὸ ἀγορασίας.

'Paying the produce' is unclear; the source says ἀποδοὺς τὸν καρπὸν τῷ Θεῷ, meaning giving the fruit/produce to God, but in context it is the value of the produce. Clarified as 'the value of the produce'.
The fragment is a Scripture lemma; joining it to the next sentence with a comma resolves the standalone issue without adding quotation marks, since the source does not mark it as a quotation.
'Buys a field from purchase' changed to 'buys a field by purchase' for idiomatic English.
The logic is clear in the source: he keeps the properties and does not give them back to others. Changed 'give them back' to 'surrender them' to avoid implying a prior transfer.
Clarified 'the produce' as 'the value of the produce' to reflect the valuation context.
